instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the launched Bonsai/Blender graphical user interface. Do not open Terminal or a shell; do not use the Blender Python console, Text editor scripts, Python, IfcOpenShell, shell commands, or any helper script/macro to directly generate or edit the deliverable file. Use only Bonsai/Blender native GUI tools, panels, menus, dialogs, and built-in save/export commands. Workshop with office shell. Start from a blank Bonsai/Blender project with no init_file inputs and no reference images. Use Bonsai's native IFC authoring workflow and save the only required deliverable on the Desktop as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc using Bonsai's graphical IFC save/export controls. Create a one-storey workshop shell with a small office, WC, and storage room. Model the building as a rectangular single-storey shell about 12 m by 7 m with walls about 3.2 m high and one floor slab. Create real IfcSpace objects named Workshop, Office, WC, Store. Include at least 8 wall-like IfcWall or IfcWallStandardCase elements, at least 1 IfcSlab, at least 4 IfcDoor elements, and at least 5 IfcWindow elements. Create real IFC/BIM elements rather than ordinary Blender mesh placeholders or visual-only geometry. The exported IFC should use the IFC4 schema and have unique GlobalId values for IfcRoot objects. Do not use IfcBuildingElementProxy objects as substitutes for the required BIM elements. The shaped model should have an overall size roughly matching the shell, with X span about 12 m, Y span about 7 m, and Z span about 3.2 m. Other coordinates, wall thicknesses, opening positions, materials, object type names, relationship nesting, property sets, and harmless exporter metadata may vary as long as the saved IFC satisfies these requirements.
